Perform Bayesian flood frequency analysis using MCMC

Source: R/full_local_regional.r
perform.analysis.Rd

Fetches climate data and annual maximum series (AMS), sets initial parameter values using probability-weighted moments (P-moments), and performs MCMC sampling for GEV parameters incorporating regional prior information.

Usage

perform.analysis(
  ams.file,
  climate.file.csv,
  is.specific.discharge = FALSE,
  num.mcmc = 1000,
  spacing = 10,
  burnin = 10000,
  num.temp = 1,
  new.reg.coef = FALSE
)

Arguments

ams.file

Character. Path to the AMS data file (one-column text or similar readable via scan).

climate.file.csv

Character. Path to the CSV file containing climate variables.

is.specific.discharge

Logical. TRUE if units are specific discharge (l/km^2/s), FALSE for total discharge (m^3/s) (default = FALSE).

num.mcmc

Integer. Number of MCMC samples to keep (default = 1000).

spacing

Integer. Thinning interval for MCMC sampling (default = 10).

burnin

Integer. Number of burn-in iterations (default = 10000).

num.temp

Integer. Number of temperatures for parallel tempering (default = 1).

new.reg.coef

Logical. If TRUE, uses updated regression coefficients (default = FALSE).

Value

A list containing:

ams

Numeric vector of original annual maxima.

clim

Data frame of standardized climate variables.

spec

Numeric vector of specific discharges.

scale

Scaling factor applied based on catchment area.

mcmc

A coda::mcmc object containing the posterior parameter samples.

is.specific.discharge

Logical indicator.
